newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: POLL-Portugal June inflation seen around 0.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Portugal June inflation seen around 0.1 pct.

text.p: The average forecast of 10 analysts polled by Reuters for Portuguese inflation in June was 0.11 percent.
Three analysts said it would stand at 0.0 percent, two said it would be 0.1 percent, two put it at 0.2 percent, two at 0.3 percent and one at -0.1 percent.
Monthly inflation rates of between -0.1 and 0.3 percent would give a year-on-year rate of between 2.0 and 2.4 percent and an average annual rate of 2.9 percent, the analysts said.
In May 1997, monthly inflation was 0.7 percent, the year-on-year rate was 2.1 percent and the average annual rate was 3.0 percent.
In June 1996, the monthly inflation rate was -0.1 percent, the year-on-year rate was 3.6 percent and the average annual rate was 3.3 percent.
The National Statistics Institute (INE) must present its monthly inflation data by the 10th working day of each month.
Analysts said the range of forecasts was wide because it was hard to estimate by how much prices would correct in June after the exceptional rises in pork and potato prices seen in May.
They said that prices in June 1996 had felt a negative impact due to the end of inflationary tensions from the "mad cow crisis".
